target_customer: Retail stock investors who share picks and research with peers
problem: Individual investors had no trusted way to build a public track record and compare ideas with peers.
business_model: advertising on a free social investing community

founders.name: Weiting Liu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Weiting Liu; TechCrunch 2006 calls him cofounder.

competitors.name: Zecco
competitors.what: Social brokerage listed as a rival

competitors.name: Bullpoo
competitors.what: Stock opinion site named as a rival in launch coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: A trade logging and rating community with market data feeds was standard web engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Reputation histories could create mild lock-in but many near-identical sites existed and the community stayed small.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TheStreet acquired competitor StockPickr; SocialPicks itself was sold to FinancialContent in 2009 and to SocialInSight in 2012 per search snippets.

market_need_then: Retail investors were active on message boards and social sites in 2006 and 2007, and several rivals raised money for social investing, per VentureBeat and TechCrunch coverage.

branding.domain_note: socialpicks.com remained live as a beta stock community when fetched in 2026.

identity.visual_style: Plain finance community layout with Research Room and Chat Room sections

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand beyond launch coverage; the name was descriptive and close to StockPickr.

outcome_analysis: SocialPicks launched in limited beta in 2006, joined YC in summer 2007 and raised about 500 thousand dollars from Bay Partners in December 2007. It never scaled beyond a small community, was sold to FinancialContent in 2009 and again to SocialInSight in 2012, and the YC page lists it inactive. No source states why it stalled, so the failure labels are inferences from many similar rivals and low traction.
notes: The 500K round is stated by VentureBeat (citing a filing); Bounce Watch lists it as a seed on 2007-12-01 with YC and Bay Partners and Seedtable labels it Series A, so the stage is other. Acquisition details (FinancialContent 2009, SocialInSight May 2012, price undisclosed) come from search result snippets of Xconomy and GlobeNewswire; Xconomy returned 503 and GlobeNewswire 403 when fetched, so I did not open them. Directory status Inactive differs from the acquired exit; the site was later relaunched under new owners. Competitor sources dated Dec 2007 are within a few months of the S07 batch. Founder spelling varies (Liu or Lu).
